title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-12-07
source: Source: sbd > Bear's cassette master  (probably) > dat (Rob Eaton) > dat (44k) - Provided by Tim Dalton; Transfer: Dat > Sony PCM-R500 > Tascam DA-3000 > wav 16/44.1 - Transferred by Charlie Miller; Lineage: wav 16/44.1 > iZotope RX6 Advanced > iZotope Ozone 5 Advanced > CD Wave >Flac16; edited and mastered SIRMick

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture with slight hiss delivers a high‑energy 1969 set highlighted by a rare Black Peter opener, dark‑star Dancin', and the primal Eleven → Love Light sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard source that suffers from a bit of hiss at the beginning but remains clear enough to enjoy. Musically the show shines with a powerful Black Peter opener, Jerry’s Dark Star‑like solo on Dancin', and the electrifying The Eleven > Love Light transition, supported by Pigpen’s top‑form vocals and harmonica. Overall the performance is high‑energy and historically interesting despite some uncertainty about the exact set order.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong show quality (high energy, standout jams) weighted at 70% yields a high score; recording is good but has minor hiss, lowering the overall rating slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: A brief hiss at the start of the Black Peter opener, otherwise clear and well‑balanced soundboard mix.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A single‑set show that blends acoustic numbers with electric jams, featuring smooth transitions (e.g., Stephen > Eleven > Love Light) and a notable Black Peter opener.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His solo on Dancin' is described as "FREAKIN DARK STAR" notes and his first solo in the Eleven > Love Light combo is highlighted as primal dead.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ adds melodic touch throughout, especially noted during the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum break between Good Lovin' segments is mentioned but not specifically praised.
